name: Trifluoperazine
metabolism: Well absorbed from the gut, but the gut wall breaks down a lot of it before it reaches the blood, so a dose by mouth leaves much less in the blood than the same dose by injection, and people differ a lot. It is broken down by hydroxylation and joining glucuronic acid, by N-oxidation, by oxidising a sulphur atom, and by dealkylation. The liver does most of this, and it leaves in the urine and faeces as a great many breakdown products, some still active, with evidence that it passes back and forth between the gut and the liver. It sticks heavily to blood proteins, spreads widely, gets into the brain more readily than into the rest of the body, crosses the placenta and passes into breast milk.
summary: Trifluoperazine is a phenothiazine typical antipsychotic used primarily to treat schizophrenia. It may also be used short term for generalized anxiety disorder.
